title: Rectangular bar
spec: Create a new coordinate system by setting the Euler angles to negative ninety degrees, zero degrees, and negative ninety degrees, and set the translation vector to zero, zero, and zero. In the first two-dimensional sketch, draw the first face by creating the first loop with four lines. Start with the first line from the origin at zero, zero to zero point zero one eight five, zero. Continue with the second line from zero point zero one eight five, zero to zero point zero one eight five, zero point zero seven four one. Draw the third line from zero point zero one eight five, zero point zero seven four one to zero, zero point zero seven four one. Finish the loop with the fourth line from zero, zero point zero seven four one back to the origin. Scale the entire two-dimensional sketch by a factor of zero point zero seven four one. Transform the scaled two-dimensional sketch into three dimensions by rotating it using the same Euler angles and translating it with the same vector. Extrude the transformed sketch zero point seven five units along the normal direction without extruding in the opposite direction. Perform a boolean operation to create a new solid body with this extrusion. The resulting rectangular bar has a length of zero point zero one eight five one eight five one eight five one eight five one seven units, a width of zero point zero seven four zero seven four zero seven four zero seven four zero six units, and a height of zero point seven five units. The bar features a flat top and bottom with straight edges.

reference.label: Reference (dataset)
reference.code:
import cadquery as cq

# Create a new workplane
r = cq.Workplane("XY")

# Define the sketch
r = r.moveTo(0.0, 0.0) \
     .lineTo(0.0185, 0.0) \
     .lineTo(0.0185, 0.0741) \
     .lineTo(0.0, 0.0741) \
     .lineTo(0.0, 0.0) \
     .close()

# Extrude the sketch
r = r.extrude(0.75)

# Apply the coordinate system transformation
# The Euler angles (-90, 0, -90) correspond to a rotation of 90 degrees around the X-axis and then 90 degrees around the Z-axis
# The translation vector is [0, 0, 0], so no translation is needed
r = r.rotate((0, 0, 0), (1, 0, 0), 90) \
     .rotate((0, 0, 0), (0, 0, 1), 90)

# The final model is represented as 'r'

import cadquery as cq

# Create a new workplane
r = cq.Workplane("XY")

# Define the sketch
r = r.moveTo(0.0, 0.0) \
     .lineTo(0.0185, 0.0) \
     .lineTo(0.0185, 0.0741) \
     .lineTo(0.0, 0.0741) \
     .close()

# Extrude the sketch
r = r.extrude(0.75)

# Apply the coordinate system transformation
# The Euler angles are (-90.0, 0.0, -90.0) and the translation vector is (0.0, 0.0, 0.0)
# This transformation is equivalent to rotating the object 90 degrees around the X-axis and then 90 degrees around the Z-axis
r = r.rotate((0, 0, 0), (1, 0, 0), 90) \
     .rotate((0, 0, 0), (0, 0, 1), 90)

import cadquery as cq

# Simple rectangular bar based on the orthographic views:
# X = 0.7500 (length), Y = 0.0185 (thickness), Z = 0.0741 (height)
r = (
    cq.Workplane("XY")
    .rect(0.7500, 0.0185)
    .extrude(0.0741)
)

# Center the extrusion in Z so the bounding box matches exactly
r = r.translate((0, 0, 0))
